description:
About the Position

Uppsala University invites applications for a doctoral student position in evolutionary and ecological genetics. The project applies genomic methods to questions in population and evolutionary genetics, studying how genetic variation is shaped by ecological processes and how natural populations adapt to changing environments.

The successful candidate joins the research environment at the Evolutionary Biology Centre (EBC), one of Europe's leading hubs for evolutionary research. The doctoral project combines laboratory genomics with computational analysis, and offers training in population genetic inference, bioinformatics and quantitative genetics within an internationally networked department.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree (or equivalent) in biology, genetics, bioinformatics or a related field, with demonstrable interest in evolutionary questions. Skills in statistical analysis and scripting are important; prior experience with sequencing data is an advantage. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed with a paid contract under collective-agreement terms, and admission runs through the university's structured doctoral programme in biology.

Highlights

  • Population and evolutionary genetics
  • Genomic analysis of natural populations
  • Adaptation to changing environments
  • Quantitative genetics and bioinformatics training
  • Research environment at the Evolutionary Biology Centre
  • Paid doctoral employment under Swedish collective agreement
